sourceTitle: 林肯之道｜移动端文本输入与信息表达体验优化

units.role: establish the project, sole-designer role, client request for systematic text optimization, and the three design questions
state delivered work, approval, implementation limits, and analytics boundary
answer question one: when input has little cost, how should limits work? same-limit versus same-rule and short-text strategy
establish the shared controlled-short-text context
show a valid Latin name rejected by current behavior
show combined nickname rules and current overflow behavior
derive how short-text form presentation and interaction work across contexts; default collapsed, expandable on click
answer question two: when the answer is unique, what matters most? why a unique identifier requires special treatment instead of a generic counter
show structured identifier input, normalization, scan, and help paths
connect identifier accuracy to owner-service value
derive why unique identifiers are least affected by product positioning; default collapsed, expandable on click
answer question three through the counting chain: connect user-perceived symbols, visible count, validation, storage, and redisplay
make multilingual and emoji counting visible to international reviewers
show preserved long text with missing proposed overflow color
show a confirmed shared allowance between body and inserted topic text
present the four-state recovery model for long text and analyze the shared allowance problem
derive how product positioning defines what counts as long text; default collapsed, expandable on click
conclude the three questions into three transferable text archetypes and six decision dimensions
consolidate archetypes and cross-cutting dimensions into a reusable decision tool
define metrics by text archetype without presenting plans as achieved results
close on the transferable design capability demonstrated by the detail
retain out-of-scope comment behavior internally without presenting it as authored work
preserve source authority and detailed section notes
retain only unresolved evidence and owner choices
